The bullseye rash, also known as erythema migrans, is a characteristic skin lesion that can appear in people infected with Lyme disease. It's typically a circular rash with a distinctive "bullseye" pattern, consisting of a red outer ring and a clear center. The rash can range in size from a few inches to over a foot in diameter. In some cases, the rash may not have a clear "bullseye" pattern, but rather appear as a solid red patch.

It's essential to note that not everyone who contracts Lyme disease will develop this rash, and its appearance can vary from person to person. Hello! I'm glad you're looking for information on Lyme disease testing. According to the CDC guidelines [1], doctors typically use a two-tiered blood testing process to help diagnose Lyme disease. The first step is an enzyme-linked immunoassay (ELISA) test, which is used as a screening tool. If the ELISA test result is positive or equivocal, a second, more specific Western blot test is then conducted to confirm the diagnosis. If the initial ELISA test result is negative, no further testing is recommended.

It's essential to note that testing is just one part of the diagnosis process, and healthcare professionals will also consider your medical history, symptoms, and other factors when determining whether you have Lyme disease.
